title: Instrumented sandbox policy for transactional tool injection in streaming executors
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: multi-tool chains in streaming mode can introduce unsafe result injection, partial commits, and inadvertent recursion when tools call back into the orchestrator or each other. Existing guard files handle recursion detection at coarse granularity and lack transactional semantics for injected results, which makes structured-output contracts brittle for long-running streams.

Goal: implement an instrumented sandbox "transaction" layer between the executor orchestrator and tool runners that: 1) buffers and validates injected tool results before they become visible to downstream steps; 2) provides commit/rollback semantics so partially-applied injections do not corrupt the streaming output; 3) exposes telemetry and tracepoints to the Console for auditing and rollback; 4) enforces recursion and loop guards deterministically and with configurable hysteresis; and 5) provides a compatibility shim for older clients that expect synchronous, immediate tool effects.

High-level approach: create a lightweight sandbox context object (opaque token per request) that travels with the streaming session. Each tool invocation runs in the sandbox; its returned artifacts are placed into a per-session tentative buffer. A small policy engine (policy-expression language) runs validation rules against each artifact: schema checks (structured-output contract), size/quota checks, and provenance assertions (origin tool, time, token). Only when a commit point is reached (explicit commit signal from orchestration or implicit commit threshold e.g., after N non-injecting tokens or end-of-turn) are buffered artifacts merged into the session's canonical output stream. Rollback can be triggered by validation failures, recursion detection, or user-configured circuit-breaker thresholds.

Key safety primitives:
- Idempotency token: per-tool-call id that must be repeatable for retries; recorded in sandbox ledger.
- Sequence fence: prevents older tool results from interleaving after a commit.
- Recursion sentinel: light-weight hop counter + signature set to detect repeated tool stacks or tool->orchestrator loops. Configurable max_hops and exponential backoff on repeated detections.
- Injection watermark: threshold-driven auto-commit for low-latency streaming (configurable per-route).
- Structured-output schema validator: pluggable validators (json-schema and protobuf) that run in sandbox and emit structured diagnostics.

Compatibility layer: for clients that call tools synchronously, the sandbox will support a strict-mode where commit is immediate (mimics current behavior) and a safe-mode where the client receives a projected view plus pending warnings. A runtime flag per-route controls this. The Console will surface routes using strict-mode to help PMs migrate.

Telemetry & observability: emit events for sandbox.create, tool.invoke.tentative, validation.error, sandbox.commit, sandbox.rollback, recursion.detected. Include token-level latency / bytes / validation-time breakdowns to aid Optimize recommendations. Audit logs capture provenance and commit diffs for compliance.

Trade-offs considered:
- Buffering introduces latency to visibility of injected results; mitigated with injection watermarks and per-route low-latency bypass for trusted tool sets.
- Stronger validation increases CPU cost; we plan to gate expensive validators behind sampling and a runtime cost budget.
- Deterministic recursion detection may require more request metadata (call stack signatures) which raises privacy considerations; we will keep signatures hashed and retention short.

Rollout plan: feature-flag behind runtime-1.20, start internal canary on dedicated pools for non-critical routes (two weeks), enable structured-output validators in read-only sampling for a week, then enable full commit semantics on a per-route opt-in with telemetry monitoring.

Docs & artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-999991+Sandbox+Policy; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1628 (WIP); Console changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/404; demo notebook: gdrive:1a2b3c-sandbox-demo

2026-03-02 - Initial design posted; asked runtime/serving to weigh in on memory impact for per-session buffers.
Action: Erik Li to run memory microbench for 1k concurrent sessions.

2026-03-04 - Design review with PM and Security. Security requested hashed provenance and 30-day retention policy. Added to spec.
Notes: keep PII out of call signatures.

2026-03-06 - Spike complete: prototype sandbox ledger and commit API implemented in local branch. Observed median extra latency 7ms for typical tool invocation (validation disabled).
PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1628

2026-03-08 - Code review feedback from Diego Ramos: 1) make sequence fences idempotent across retries; 2) add explicit test harness for rollback during streaming; 3) prefer async commit hook to avoid blocking IO threads. Implementing changes now.

2026-03-09 - Integration tests: added schema fuzz tests and recursion stress test; discovered a path where tool A calling tool B then orchestration callback produced a loop due to missing hop increment. Fix submitted in PR.
2026-03-10 - PM sign-off requested for compatibility mode UX in Console. PM suggests a migration guide and telemetry dashboard before opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox context created per streaming session and included in 100% of tool invocations in canary routes.
Tentative buffer held until commit/rollback; no tentative artifact becomes canonical before commit.
Recursion sentinel triggers after configured hop threshold and prevents further tool invocations from mutating session state.
Structured-output validator runs on tentative artifacts and surface diagnostics in Console with per-token telemetry.
Compatibility mode toggles replicate legacy behavior; migrations documented in Console and developer docs.
risks_mitigation: Increased latency: mitigate with injection watermarks and trusted-tool bypass rule; measure and document cost to Optimize team.
Resource blowup from large buffers: cap per-session buffer and evict old tentative artifacts using LRU policy; fail open to rollback on eviction.
False-positive recursion detection: allow a grace window and exponential backoff to prevent noisy circuit trips.
test_plan: Unit tests for sandbox ledger (create/append/commit/rollback) covering idempotent retries.
Integration tests for streaming executor with tentative injections and watermarks under varying message rates.
Chaos test: induce tool timeouts and verify rollback semantics and audit logs contain useful diffs.
Recursion fuzz test: random tool-call graphs with hop limits to ensure detection and graceful degradation.
Performance benchmark: 1k concurrent sessions with schema validation sampling enabled to quantify CPU cost.
